To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we demonstrate a memristive synapse with gradual potentiation and degradation, which are easy-to-be-implemented on-chip; 2) we demonstrate a STDP-like learning rule for memristive synapses, that can be used for the implementation of SNN; 3) we simulate a simple SNN for pattern recognition, which is able to learn and classify different patterns.
we propose a HfO2-based resistive memory device that can be used for STDP implementation, and that we demonstrate the capability of such a device to emulate a SNN for pattern recognition.

we demonstrate the possibility to implement a neuromorphic circuit by using a TiN/ HF O2/Ti/TIN memristor as a basic building block, and that this circuit is able to perform a pattern recognition task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of HfO2-based devices that can emulate the behavior of biological synapses.
the development of memristive devices for neuromorphic computing.
the development of a novel memristor-based artificial synapse, which is able to emulate the biological learning process and can be used for neuromorphic computing applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed memristor can be used as a building block of a SNN for pattern recognition.
the proposed HfO2-based device is a promising candidate to implement artificial synapse in neuromorphic architectures.

we have demonstrated a memristive device that, by virtue of its electrical behavior, can be considered as a suitable candidate as artificial synapse to emulate the learning process of biological neurons in neuromorphic architectures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single device can emulate the biological learning process and implement a simple pattern recognition algorithm, paving the road for future neuromorphic applications based on memristors.
we propose a memristor device that can be used as artificial synapse to implement STDP in neuromorphic architectures.
we demonstrated the possibility of using a memristive synapse for implementing STDP learning in a SNN, thus paving the way for the realization of neuromorphic architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
memristors can be used as artificial synapses for neuromorphic systems.
memristors can implement STDP and can be exploited for neuromorphic computing applications.
memristors are promising candidates for the implementation of neuromorphic systems.
